diagnostic_evidence.quote: $A$ and $Q$ have eigenvalues $\mu_k = r^{-1}(\kappa^2 + \xi_k)^{\alpha}$ and $\lambda_k = \sigma r^{-\gamma}(\kappa^2 + \xi_k)^{-\beta}$

issues.failure_explanation: From $\xi_k \ge C_\Delta k^{2/d}$ one gets $\mu_k \ge r^{-1}\xi_k^\alpha \ge r^{-1}C_\Delta^{\alpha}k^{2\alpha/d}$ and $\lambda_k \le \sigma r^{-\gamma}C_\Delta^{-\beta}k^{-2\beta/d}$, i.e. $C_1 = r^{-1}C_\Delta^{\alpha}$ and $C_2 = \sigma r^{-\gamma}C_\Delta^{-\beta}$, not $r^{-1}C_\Delta$ and $\sigma r^{-\gamma}C_\Delta$ as the proof asserts (the asserted bounds are false for general $\alpha,\beta$, e.g. $C_\Delta<1$, $\alpha>1$). Consequently the explicit constant $C_\Delta^{2-2\gamma}$ in the corollary should be $C_\Delta^{-\beta-(2\gamma-1)\alpha}$; the stated constant is only correct when $\alpha=\beta=1$.

failure_location.quote: satisfy the bounds $r^{-1} C_\Delta k^{\frac{2 \alpha}{d}}\leq \mu_k$ and $\lambda_k \leq \sigma r^{-\gamma} C_\Delta k^{- \frac{2 \beta}{d}}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $C_1,C_2$ by $r^{-1}C_\Delta^{\alpha}$ and $\sigma r^{-\gamma}C_\Delta^{-\beta}$ and the constant by $\frac{\sigma r^{\gamma-1}C_\Delta^{-\beta-(2\gamma-1)\alpha}\Gamma(2\gamma-1)}{\Gamma(\gamma)^2}\frac{d}{2\nu}$.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence rate $M^{-2\nu/d}$ in Corollary 3.3 is unaffected, but the advertised explicit constant is wrong for the general parameters $\alpha,\beta$ the corollary claims to cover.
issues.title: Wrong eigenvalue constants C_1, C_2 in Corollary 3.3 give an incorrect explicit constant
issues.why_classification: A local recomputation of the constant fixes the statement; rate, method and scope all survive.

issues.failure_explanation: All four parts of the proof bound the square root of the mean-square error by $\frac{\sqrt{\lambda_k}}{\Gamma(\gamma)}(\ldots)h^{\min(\gamma-1/2,m+1)}$ (with factor $\mu_k^{-1/q}$ in Part 2 and $(1+\sqrt{\log(th^{-1})})$ in Part 4). Squaring yields $\lambda_k$, $\mu_k^{-2/q}$ and $(1+\sqrt{\log(th^{-1})})^2$, but the theorem states $\sqrt{\lambda_k}$, $\mu_k^{-1/q}$ and the unsquared $\delta_{\gamma,h}$. The stated bound is actually false: the mean-square error scales exactly linearly in $\lambda_k$ while $C(C_\Pi,t,\gamma)$ is independent of $\lambda_k$, so for large $\lambda_k$ the claim $\le\sqrt{\lambda_k}C h^{\ldots}$ fails; likewise for $\gamma=m+3/2$ the true $L^2$ best-approximation error squared behaves like $h^{2m+2}\log(t/h)$, exceeding $\sqrt{\log(t/h)}h^{2m+2}$ for small $h$. Theorem 3.9 uses $\lambda_k$ and $\mu_k^{-2/q}$ (consistent with the proof) but inherits the unsquared $\delta_{\gamma,h}$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the bounds with $\lambda_k$ in place of $\sqrt{\lambda_k}$, $\mu_k^{-2/q}$ in place of $\mu_k^{-1/q}$, and $\delta_{\gamma,h}^2$ (or $1+\log(th^{-1})$) in place of $\delta_{\gamma,h}$, in Theorem 3.4, Corollaries 3.5, 3.8 and Theorem 3.9.
issues.overall_effect: The stated temporal error bounds in Theorem 3.4, Corollaries 3.5 and 3.8 are not what is proved and are false as written in the dependence on $\lambda_k$ (and on the log factor when $\gamma=m+3/2$); Theorem 3.9's log factor is likewise unsupported. The $h$-rate itself is established.
issues.title: Theorem 3.4 states the root-mean-square bound as a mean-square bound (missing squares on $\sqrt{\lambda_k}$, $\mu_k^{-1/q}$, $\delta_{\gamma,h}$)
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the statements to what the proofs actually give preserves the convergence orders and all guarantees up to constants/log-power.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: & \leq C_{\Pi}^2 \sum_{\ell = 1}^n \left[ g_\ell^2 (t_\ell - t_{\ell - 1}) + 2 \alpha g_\ell \int_{t_{\ell - 1}}^{t_\ell} f_{t_n}(s) \, \text{d}s + \alpha^2 \int_{t_{\ell - 1}}^{t_\ell} f_{t_n}(s)^2 \, \text{d}s  \right]

issues.failure_explanation: The proof expands $\|\Pi_0(g+\alpha f)\|^2$ and $\|g+\alpha f\|^2$ into per-interval terms $g_\ell^2 h_\ell$, a cross term $2\alpha g_\ell(\cdot)$ and an $\alpha^2(\cdot)$ term, and then bounds each term separately by a constant times the corresponding term of $\|g+\alpha f\|^2$ with constant $1$ for the first, and constants from Lemma 3.10 for the others. This is invalid: the cross term has the sign of $\alpha g_\ell$, and when $\alpha g_\ell<0$ the inequality $2\alpha g_\ell X \lesssim 2\alpha g_\ell Y$ with $X\asymp Y$ requires $X\ge C Y$, which fails for $C$ larger than the comparability ratio (e.g. $\gamma>1$, $\theta=0$, where $X=h_\ell f(t_{\ell-1})\ge Y=\int_{I_\ell}f$ but $X\le CY$ with $C>1$ does not give $2\alpha g_\ell X\le C\,2\alpha g_\ell Y$). Moreover the displayed step bounds a difference $A-B$ of two quantities by comparing $A\lesssim A'$ and $B\gtrsim B'$ with different constants, which does not yield $A-B\lesssim A'-B'$ when $A'-B'=\int_{I_\ell}f\ll A'$. Summing termwise bounds with different constants across indefinite terms does not give $\|\Pi_0 h\|^2\le C_\Pi^2\|h\|^2$. The lemma's conclusion is plausibly true (on each interval the ratio is a sup over the two-dimensional space span$\{1,f|_{I_\ell}\}$ and can be bounded uniformly using quasi-uniformity), but the given argument does not establish it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the termwise argument with a per-interval argument: write $h|_{I_\ell}=(g_\ell+\alpha\bar f_\ell)+\alpha(f-\bar f_\ell)$ with $\bar f_\ell$ the interval mean, use $\|\Pi_0 h\|^2_{I_\ell}=h_\ell(g_\ell+\alpha f(\tilde s_\ell))^2\le (1+\eta)h_\ell(g_\ell+\alpha\bar f_\ell)^2+(1+1/\eta)\alpha^2 h_\ell (f(\tilde s_\ell)-\bar f_\ell)^2$, and prove $h_\ell(f(\tilde s_\ell)-\bar f_\ell)^2\le C\int_{I_\ell}(f-\bar f_\ell)^2$ uniformly in $\ell$ via the comparability estimates of Lemma 3.10 and a scaling argument on the last interval.
issues.overall_effect: The $L^2$-stability constant $C_\Pi$ for the point-evaluation operator $\Pi_0$ is not established, so Corollary 3.8 (convergence of the left-point/theta method), whose proof is a direct application of Lemma 3.7 and Theorem 3.4, is unsupported as written.
issues.title: Proof of Lemma 3.7 bounds indefinite cross terms termwise, ignoring the sign of $\alpha g_\ell$
issues.why_classification: The conclusion appears recoverable without changing any rate or scope, but a genuinely new (if contained) replacement argument handling the sign of the cross term is required.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We can derive an error bound for the full discretisation by combining \Cref{thm:spectral-convergence} and \Cref{thm-convergence}. A more detailed proof can found in \Cref{sec:proofs}.

issues.failure_explanation: Under the theorem's own hypothesis $1+r_\lambda-(2\gamma-1)r_\mu<0$ the stated constant $C'$ is strictly negative, so the spatial term $C' M^{-2\nu/d}$ is negative and the stated bound is not what Theorem 3.1 provides (which has the positive constant $\frac{d}{2\nu}=-(1+r_\lambda-(2\gamma-1)r_\mu)^{-1}$). In addition, the text promises a detailed proof in Section 5, but Section 5 contains no proof of Theorem 3.9; the needed step (orthogonality of $X-\tilde X_M$ and $\tilde X_M-\tilde X^h_M$ in $L^2(\mathcal D)$ so that the two errors add, and summation of Theorem 3.4 over $k\le M$) is never written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $C'$ by the constant $C$ of Theorem 3.1 (i.e. divide by $-(1+r_\lambda-(2\gamma-1)r_\mu)$) and add the one-paragraph proof: $\mathbb E\|X-\tilde X^h_M\|^2=\mathbb E\|X-\tilde X_M\|^2+\sum_{k\le M}\mathbb E|c_k-\tilde c_k|^2$ by orthogonality of the eigenfunctions, then apply Theorems 3.1 and 3.4.
issues.overall_effect: The main theorem's explicit spatial constant is wrong in sign, and its proof is not actually supplied; the result is nonetheless recoverable from Theorems 3.1 and 3.4.
issues.title: Theorem 3.9: stated spatial constant $C'$ is negative and the promised proof is absent
issues.why_classification: The sign correction is local and the missing proof is a routine orthogonality-plus-summation argument; all rates and guarantees survive.
